author: David Leisering
title: Justin Dean triples for first major league hit Friday
desc: Justin Dean went 1-for-2 with a bases-clearing triple on Friday, helping the Cubs to a 16-2 win over the Blue Jays.
impact: After 745 games and more than 3,000 plate appearances in the minors, Dean tripled with the bases loaded in the seventh on Friday for his first career major league hit. Dean was hitting .238 with 14 stolen bases at Triple-A Iowa prior to his call-up and is a lifetime .251 hitter in the minors with 42 home runs and 253 stolen bases during his eight-year minor league career. While Dean, more than likely, won't play enough to be fantasy relevant, this was a day he won't forget and was one of the feel good moments of the season.

author: Nate Miller
title: Martin Perez turns in a terrific performance Friday night
desc: Martin Perez allowed one run on six hits and one walk while striking out five over six innings in Friday's 3-2 win over the Brewers.
impact: Given an extra day to rest after Thursday's rain out, Perez delivered an excellent effort for the Braves just when they needed one Friday night. The 35-year-old lefty has now gone at least five innings while giving up three runs or less in five straight outings, posting a 2.66 ERA and 1.15 WHIP across 27 innings in that stretch. Perez has been a real asset in the Braves' rotation during the first half.

author: David Leisering
title: Dansby Swanson swipes two bags in Friday victory
desc: Dansby Swanson went 1-for-4 with two runs scored, two walks, two stolen bases, and an RBI on Friday during the Cubs' 16-2 win over Toronto.
impact: Swanson stole his eighth and ninth bases of the season on Friday and he has been yet to get caught attempting to steal all year. The veteran has eight home runs and nine stolen bases on the year but, overall, it has been a massively disappointing season as he is hitting just .177 with a .601 OPS across 72 games.

author: Nate Miller
title: Raisel Iglesias shaky while picking up 15th save
desc: Raisel Iglesias allowed one run on two hits and a walk while striking out one en route to a save in Friday's 3-2 win over the Brewers.
impact: Iglesias was certainly not on cruise control Friday night, and it took a brilliant throw from left field to home by Eli White to preserve the save for the veteran closer and a win for the Braves. Iglesias is now up to 15 saves with a still stellar 1.48 ERA, but he has been playing with fire much more recently than he did earlier in the season.

author: Nate Miller
title: Mike Yastrzemski smacks solo shot in Friday's win
desc: Mike Yastrzemski went 1-for-3 with a solo homer in Friday's 3-2 win over the Brewers.
impact: Yastrzemski was certainly in need of a big a hit, and he delivered his first one in quite some time during the seventh inning of Friday's win. The veteran outfielder came into the game hitting an ugly .139 in June and had not homered in nearly a full month's time. Perhaps Friday's big fly can get Yastrzemski going again.

author: David Leisering
title: Carson Kelly belts grand slam in blowout win Friday
desc: Carson Kelly went 2-for-4 with a grand slam home run to help the Cubs to a 16-2 blowout victory over the Blue Jays on Friday.
impact: Kelly hit his grand slam as part of a seven-run first inning for the Cubs against Toronto starter, Kevin Gausman. The catcher reached base four times, adding a pair of walks, and finished with three runs scored and six runs batted in. Kelley is batting .282 with four home runs and 26 RBI in 56 games this season.

author: David Leisering
title: Pete Crow-Armstrong reaches five times, steals two bags Friday
desc: Pete Crow-Armstrong went 3-for-3 with a pair of walks and two stolen bases on Friday as the Cubs hammered the Blue Jays, 16-2.
impact: Crow-Armstrong extended his hitting streak to nine straight and has now hit safely in 21 of his last 22 games, raising his season average from .223 to .283 during that span. All three of his hits were singles on Friday and his stolen bases were his 17th and 18th of the season - tied for third-most in the National League. Crow-Armstrong is on another level at the moment as he is hitting .433 (29-for-67) with eight home runs and six stolen bases this month. PCA has been even better over the last week, batting .517 (15-for-29) with six runs scored, three doubles, one triple, four home runs, six RBI, and three stolen bases in his last seven games.

author: David Leisering
title: Ben Brown goes six in fourth win of season Friday
desc: Ben Brown allowed two runs on four hits, did not walk a batter, and struck out four as the Cubs hammered the Blue Jays, 16-2, on Friday.
impact: Brown continued his sensational work since joining the Cubs' rotation as he has now allowed three runs or fewer in all eight of his starts. He did allow his first home run in 42.1 innings as a starter - and just his second of the season - to George Springer in the sixth. Brown has allowed just eight earned runs in his eight starts and sports a 3-1 record with a 1.70 ERA and a 41:11 K:BB ratio in those outings. Overall, in 20 appearances, he is 4-2 with a 1.85 ERA and a 65:19 K:BB ratio across 68 innings. Brown is lined up to take on the Mets, in New York, in his next start on Wednesday.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Bryan Reynolds (groin) scratched from lineup Friday
desc: Bryan Reynolds was a late scratch from the Pirates starting lineup on Friday night due to left groin discomfort.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Shohei Ohtani to go on paternity list
desc: The Dodgers are expected to place Shohei Ohtani on the paternity list.
impact: Ohtani will be away for a few days. He should be back early next week.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Blake Snell (elbow) close to first bullpen
desc: Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Blake Snell is close to throwing his first bullpen session.
impact: Snell is working his way back from surgery to remove bone chips from his pitching elbow. He'll likely be activated after the All-Star break.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Luke Raley (flu) not in lineup Friday
desc: Luke Raley is not in the Mariners lineup on Friday against the Red Sox.
impact: Raley remains day-to-day with an illness.

author: Chris Schommer
title: Trey Yesavage steady on mound in win over Red Sox
desc: Trey Yesavage allowed three earned runs on four hits while striking out six over 7 1/3 innings in Thursday's win over the Red Sox.
impact: Yesavage has struggled to miss opposing bats of late, allowing three earned runs or more in four of his last five starts. The right-hander has offered manager John Schneider one of many inconsistent options in the Blue Jays rotation to this point, posting a 3.76 ERA and 1.16 WHIP with a 3-3 record and 8.7 K/9 ratio through 10 starts.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Teoscar Hernandez (hamstring) could begin rehab assignment next week
desc: Teoscar Hernandez could be cleared to begin a rehab assignment next week.
impact: Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Hernandez will go on a rehab assignment when the team is on the road next. That starts on Monday against the Twins.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Edwin Diaz (elbow) throws 15 pitches in bullpen session Friday
desc: Edwin Diaz threw a successful 15-pitch bullpen session on Friday.
impact: Diaz threw off the mound for the first time since his surgery. He'll continue to throw bullpens until he is cleared to face live hitters.
